about: Vendor bidding beside surrogate bidding (Aanya, 27 Oct 2026): publish an event, invite 2-3 vendors, the buyer enters a surrogate response for one, another vendor signs in to the vendor portal (shown beside the buyer's page) and responds, and the buyer sees both. RFQ, RFP, RFP+RFQ, auction, RFQ+auction, plus a counter offer across the two tabs. Judged by the run and Procol's own records: a surrogate response is placed by the event's creator, a vendor-portal one by the vendor's user.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. Place a surrogate bid of 100 for one vendor, then the other vendor logs into the vendor portal and bids 90. The buyer should see both responses: one marked Surrogate Bid and one from the vendor portal.
cases.note: the basic mix: one surrogate, one from the portal
cases.must: RFQ published to 2 vendors; one surrogate bid (100) and one vendor-portal bid (90); the buyer's Responses show both.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 3 vendors and publish it. Place a surrogate bid for one vendor and have a second vendor bid from the vendor portal; the third vendor does not bid. The buyer should see 2 responses and participation 2 of 3.
cases.must: RFQ published to 3 vendors; one surrogate and one vendor-portal bid; the buyer sees 2 responses, participation 2/3.

cases.prompt: Create a technical-only RFP event, invite 2 vendors and publish it. Submit a surrogate technical response for one vendor, then the other vendor logs into the vendor portal and submits its technical response. The buyer should see both responses on the technical stage.
cases.note: RFP: technical answers, one surrogate, one from the portal
cases.must: Technical-only event published to 2 vendors; one surrogate and one vendor-portal technical response; the buyer sees both on the technical stage.

cases.prompt: Create an RFP + RFQ event with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. One vendor logs into the vendor portal, submits its technical response and then quotes 95 on the RFQ. For the other vendor the buyer submits a surrogate technical response and a surrogate bid of 100. The buyer should see both vendors on the technical stage and on the RFQ.
cases.note: two-stage: the portal vendor answers the technical sheet first, then quotes
cases.must: Technical + RFQ event, 2 vendors; each stage has one surrogate and one vendor-portal response; the buyer sees both on each stage.

cases.prompt: Create a reverse auction with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. Place a surrogate bid of 100 for one vendor, then the other vendor logs into the vendor portal and bids 90. The buyer should see both bids.
cases.note: auction: one surrogate, one live from the portal
cases.must: Auction published to 2 vendors; one surrogate bid and one vendor-portal bid; the buyer sees both.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ + auction event (the RFQ first, the auction after it) with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. On the RFQ, place a surrogate bid for one vendor and have the other vendor bid from the vendor portal. The buyer should see both responses on the RFQ.
cases.note: combination: Procol keeps RFQ and auction apart, so the RFQ is converted to an auction after the bids (the auction stage carries the RFQ's two bids over, so bids are counted per vendor, not per stage)
cases.must: RFQ published to 2 vendors; one surrogate and one vendor-portal bid on it, both seen by the buyer; then Convert to Auction.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. Both vendors log into the vendor portal one after the other and bid 100 and 90. The buyer should see 2 responses, neither marked Surrogate Bid.
cases.note: two vendors from the portal, no surrogate
cases.must: RFQ published to 2 vendors; both bid from the vendor portal; the buyer sees 2 responses, none surrogate.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. The buyer places a surrogate bid of 120 for one vendor and the other vendor bids 100 from the vendor portal. In Master QCS the vendor-portal bid of 100 should rank first.
cases.note: ranks across a surrogate and a portal bid
cases.must: RFQ, 2 vendors; surrogate 120 and portal 100; Master QCS ranks the 100 bid first.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 1 vendor and publish it. The vendor bids 100 from the vendor portal, the buyer sends a counter offer of 90, the vendor accepts it in the vendor portal, and the buyer sees the counter offer accepted.
cases.note: counter offer across the two tabs
cases.must: RFQ, 1 vendor; a vendor-portal bid, a counter offer of 90 from the buyer, accepted by the vendor; the buyer's grid marks it accepted.

cases.prompt: Create an RFQ with 1 line item, invite 2 vendors and publish it. First one vendor logs into the vendor portal and bids 100, then the buyer places a surrogate bid of 110 for the other vendor. The buyer should see both responses.
cases.note: the other order: portal first, then the surrogate bid for the other vendor
cases.must: RFQ, 2 vendors; a vendor-portal bid then a surrogate bid for the other vendor; the buyer sees both.
